answer: One defence is to bind every identity to a physical root of trust. Each node carries a secure element whose key is fused into silicon at manufacture; the registry enrols that key once and refuses a second enrolment from the same die, so minting a thousand puppets costs a thousand chips, not keystrokes. Attestation lands at dawn, when nodes sign the epoch seed; a cloned key cannot fork without a second signature. The seal is ferrous literally: a metal can with a tamper mesh, so copying leaves traces. A lagoon of idle agents is harmless; the tax falls on duplication, not participation.
